key_insight: A confidence-aware LLM system, DIAGNO, matched or outperformed neurologists when both were judged against autopsy-confirmed neuropathology across diverse complex neurological cases.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests AI could support differential diagnosis in challenging neurology cases, but it is a decision-support tool rather than a substitute for expert clinical evaluation.
method: Built NeuroBench from 791 retrospective cases with neuropathology-confirmed diagnoses across 3 health systems
Had DIAGNO generate top-3 differentials, using retrieval-augmented generation for lower-confidence cases
Compared DIAGNO with neurologists in a blinded subset using adjudicators against ground truth
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, DIAGNO reached 83.8% top-3 accuracy at MGH, 76.5% at Mount Sinai, and 92.3% at UTHSA; in 203 complex MGH cases it slightly outperformed neurologists on top-3 and taxonomy-level accuracy.
watch_item: The benchmark is retrospective and neurology-specific, so performance may not directly translate to real-time practice, different specialties, or settings without neuropathology-confirmed ground truth.
paper_title: Assessing AI and Neurologist Diagnostic Reasoning Against Neuropathological Ground Truth
